C0000.summary: The chief executive officer of a State desiring to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title must designate, in an application submitted to the Secretary under subsection (b), an appropriate State agency that complies with the requirements of paragraph (2) to act as a lead agency for purposes of carrying out State activities under this chapter.

C0001.summary: The lead agency must develop the State plan to be submitted to the Secretary under subsection (b).

C0002.summary: The lead agency must, in conjunction with the development of the State plan as required under subsection (b), hold at least one hearing in the State with sufficient time and statewide distribution of notice of such hearing, to provide to the public an opportunity to comment on the proposed use and distribution of funds to be provided through the grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title for the period covered by the State plan.

C0003.summary: The lead agency must conduct reviews of eligible entities under section 9914 of this title.

C0004.summary: In order to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the State must hold at least one legislative hearing every 3 years in conjunction with the development of the State plan.
C0004.scope_text: In order to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0005.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, a State must prepare and submit to the Secretary an application and State plan covering a period of not less than 1 fiscal year and not more than 2 fiscal years, submitted not later than 30 days prior to the beginning of the first fiscal year covered by the plan, and containing such information as the Secretary shall require, including the specified assurances and descriptions.
C0005.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0006.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain an assurance that funds made available through the grant or allotment will be used to support activities designed to assist low-income families and individuals—including families and individuals receiving assistance under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act, homeless families and individuals, migrant or seasonal farmworkers, and elderly low-income individuals and families—and a description of how such activities will enable the families and individuals to remove obstacles and solve problems that block self-sufficiency (including for those transitioning off part A of title IV of the Social Security Act), secure and retain meaningful employment, attain an adequate education (with particular attention to improving literacy skills, which may include family literacy initiatives), make better use of available income, obtain and maintain adequate housing and suitable living environment, obtain emergency assistance through loans, grants, or other means, and achieve greater participation in community affairs (including grassroots partnerships to document best practices and strengthen relationships with local law enforcement agencies, such as community policing).
C0006.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0007.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain an assurance that funds made available through the grant or allotment will be used to address the needs of youth in low-income communities through youth development programs that support the primary role of the family, give priority to the prevention of youth problems and crime, promote increased community coordination and collaboration in meeting youth needs, and support development and expansion of innovative community-based youth development programs demonstrating success in preventing or reducing youth crime, such as violence-free zone programs (involving youth mediation, mentoring, life skills training, job creation, and entrepreneurship) and after-school child care programs.
C0007.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0008.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain an assurance that funds made available through the grant or allotment will be used to make more effective use of, and to coordinate with, other programs related to the purposes of this chapter (including State welfare reform efforts).
C0008.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0009.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain a description of how the State intends to use discretionary funds made available from the remainder of the grant or allotment described in section 9907(b) of this title in accordance with this chapter, including a description of how the State will support innovative community and neighborhood-based initiatives related to the purposes of this chapter.
C0009.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0010.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain information provided by eligible entities in the State, containing a description of the service delivery system targeted to low-income individuals and families, a description of how linkages will be developed to fill service gaps, a description of how grant funds under section 9907(a) will be coordinated with other resources, and a description of how the local entity will use the funds to support innovative community and neighborhood-based initiatives (which may include fatherhood and family strengthening initiatives).
C0010.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0011.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain an assurance that eligible entities in the State will provide, on an emergency basis, for the provision of such supplies and services, nutritious foods, and related services, as may be necessary to counteract conditions of starvation and malnutrition among low-income individuals.
C0011.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0012.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain an assurance that the State and the eligible entities in the State will coordinate and establish linkages between governmental and other social services programs to assure effective delivery and avoid duplication, and a description of how the State and eligible entities will coordinate employment and training activities (as defined in section 3 of the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act) with entities providing activities through statewide and local workforce development systems under such Act.
C0012.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0013.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain an assurance that the State will ensure coordination between antipoverty programs in each community in the State, and ensure, where appropriate, that emergency energy crisis intervention programs under title XXVI (relating to low-income home energy assistance) are conducted in such community.
C0013.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0014.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain an assurance that the State will permit and cooperate with Federal investigations undertaken in accordance with section 9916 of this title.
C0014.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0015.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain an assurance that any eligible entity in the State that received funding in the previous fiscal year through a community services block grant made under this chapter will not have its funding terminated under this chapter, or reduced below the proportional share of funding it received in the previous fiscal year, unless, after notice and an opportunity for a hearing on the record, the State determines that cause exists for such termination or reduction, subject to review by the Secretary as provided in section 9915(b) of this title.
C0015.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0016.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain an assurance that the State and eligible entities in the State will, to the maximum extent possible, coordinate programs with and form partnerships with other organizations serving low-income residents of the communities and members of the groups served by the State, including religious organizations, charitable groups, and community organizations.
C0016.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0017.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain an assurance that the State will require each eligible entity in the State to establish procedures under which a low-income individual, community organization, religious organization, or representative of low-income individuals that considers itself or low-income individuals inadequately represented on the board (or other mechanism) of the eligible entity may petition for adequate representation.
C0017.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0018.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain an assurance that the State will secure from each eligible entity in the State, as a condition to receipt of funding by the entity through a community services block grant under this chapter for a program, a community action plan (which shall be submitted to the Secretary, at the request of the Secretary, with the State plan) that includes a community-needs assessment for the community served, which may be coordinated with community-needs assessments conducted for other programs.
C0018.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0019.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain an assurance that the State and all eligible entities in the State will, not later than fiscal year 2001, participate in the Results Oriented Management and Accountability System, another performance measure system developed pursuant to section 9917(b), or an alternative system meeting section 9917(b) requirements, and a description of outcome measures to measure eligible entity performance in promoting self-sufficiency, family stability, and community revitalization.
C0019.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0020.summary: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, as part of the State application and plan to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the plan must contain information describing how the State will carry out the assurances described in subsection (b).
C0020.scope_text: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

C0021.summary: For purposes of making a determination in accordance with subsection (b)(8) with respect to a funding reduction, the term “cause” includes a statewide redistribution of funds provided through a community services block grant under this chapter to respond to the results of the most recently available census or other appropriate data, the designation of a new eligible entity, or severe economic dislocation; or the failure of an eligible entity to comply with the terms of an agreement or a State plan, or to meet a State requirement, as described in section 9915(a) of this title.
C0021.scope_text: For purposes of making a determination in accordance with subsection (b)(8) with respect to a funding reduction

C0022.summary: For purposes of making a determination in accordance with subsection (b)(8) with respect to a termination, the term “cause” includes the failure of an eligible entity to comply with the terms of an agreement or a State plan, or to meet a State requirement, as described in section 9915(a) of this title.
C0022.scope_text: For purposes of making a determination in accordance with subsection (b)(8) with respect to a termination

C0023.summary: The Secretary may prescribe procedures for the purpose of assessing the effectiveness of eligible entities in carrying out the purposes of this chapter.

C0024.summary: The chief executive officer of each State may revise any plan prepared under this section.

C0025.summary: The chief executive officer of each State must submit any revised plan prepared under this section to the Secretary.

C0026.summary: Each plan or revised plan prepared under this section must be made available for public inspection within the State in such a manner as will facilitate review of, and comment on, the plan.

C0027.summary: For fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, a State must prepare and submit to the Secretary an application and State plan in accordance with the provisions of this chapter (as in effect on the day before October 27, 1998), rather than the provisions of subsections (a) through (c) relating to applications and plans.
C0027.scope_text: For fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title

inventory.U0000: To receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the chief executive officer of a State must designate an appropriate State agency that complies with the duties specified in paragraph (2) to act as the lead agency for carrying out State activities under this chapter, designating it in an application submitted to the Secretary under subsection (b).
inventory.U0001: The designated State lead agency must develop the State plan to be submitted to the Secretary under subsection (b).
inventory.U0002: In conjunction with developing the State plan under subsection (b), the designated State lead agency must hold at least one hearing in the State with sufficient time and statewide distribution of notice, giving the public an opportunity to comment on the proposed use and distribution of funds provided through the grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 for the period covered by the State plan.
inventory.U0003: The designated State lead agency must conduct reviews of eligible entities under section 9914 of this title.
inventory.U0004: In order to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, the State must hold at least one legislative hearing every 3 years in conjunction with the development of the State plan.
inventory.U0005: Beginning with fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906 of this title, a State must prepare and submit to the Secretary an application and State plan covering a period of not less than 1 fiscal year and not more than 2 fiscal years, submitted not later than 30 days prior to the beginning of the first fiscal year covered by the plan, containing such information as the Secretary requires, including paragraphs (1) through (13).
inventory.U0006: The State application and plan must contain an assurance that grant or allotment funds will be used to support activities designed to assist low-income families and individuals (including those receiving TANF assistance under part A of title IV of the Social Security Act, homeless families and individuals, migrant or seasonal farmworkers, and elderly low-income individuals and families), and a description of how such activities will enable them to remove obstacles and solve problems that block self-sufficiency (including transitioning off a State part A title IV program).
inventory.U0007: The State plan must include a description of how supported activities will enable low-income families and individuals to secure and retain meaningful employment.
inventory.U0008: The State plan must include a description of how supported activities will enable low-income families and individuals to attain an adequate education, with particular attention toward improving literacy skills of low-income families in the communities involved, which may include carrying out family literacy initiatives.
inventory.U0009: The State plan must include a description of how supported activities will enable low-income families and individuals to make better use of available income.
inventory.U0010: The State plan must include a description of how supported activities will enable low-income families and individuals to obtain and maintain adequate housing and a suitable living environment.
inventory.U0011: The State plan must include a description of how supported activities will enable low-income families and individuals to obtain emergency assistance through loans, grants, or other means to meet immediate and urgent family and individual needs.
inventory.U0012: The State plan must include a description of how supported activities will enable low-income families and individuals to achieve greater participation in community affairs, including developing public and private grassroots partnerships with local law enforcement, housing authorities, private foundations, and others to document urban grassroots best practices for widespread replication, and to strengthen relationships with local law enforcement (which may include neighborhood or community policing efforts).
inventory.U0013: The State plan must contain an assurance that funds will be used to address youth needs in low-income communities through youth development programs that support the family's primary role, prioritize prevention of youth problems and crime, promote community coordination and collaboration, and support innovative community-based youth programs demonstrated to reduce youth crime, such as violence-free zones with intervention models (mediation, mentoring, life skills, job creation, entrepreneurship) and after-school child care programs.
inventory.U0014: The State plan must contain an assurance that grant or allotment funds will be used to make more effective use of, and coordinate with, other programs related to the purposes of this chapter, including State welfare reform efforts.
inventory.U0015: The State plan must contain a description of how the State intends to use discretionary funds from the remainder of the grant or allotment under section 9907(b) in accordance with this chapter, including how it will support innovative community- and neighborhood-based initiatives related to chapter purposes.
inventory.U0016: The State plan must include information provided by eligible entities in the State describing the service delivery system for services provided or coordinated with section 9907(a) funds targeted to low-income individuals and families.
inventory.U0017: The State plan must include information provided by eligible entities describing how linkages will be developed to fill identified service gaps through information, referrals, case management, and followup consultations.
inventory.U0018: The State plan must include information provided by eligible entities describing how section 9907(a) grant funds will be coordinated with other public and private resources.
inventory.U0019: The State plan must include information provided by eligible entities describing how the local entity will use funds to support innovative community- and neighborhood-based initiatives related to chapter purposes, which may include fatherhood initiatives and other family-strengthening and parenting initiatives.
inventory.U0020: The State plan must contain an assurance that eligible entities in the State will provide, on an emergency basis, supplies, services, nutritious foods, and related services necessary to counteract starvation and malnutrition among low-income individuals.
inventory.U0021: The State plan must contain an assurance that the State and eligible entities will coordinate and establish linkages between governmental and other social services programs to assure effective delivery and avoid duplication, as well as a description of how they will coordinate employment and training activities (as defined under section 3 of WIOA) with entities providing activities through statewide and local workforce development systems under WIOA.
inventory.U0022: The State plan must contain an assurance that the State will ensure coordination between antipoverty programs in each community, and ensure, where appropriate, that emergency energy crisis intervention programs under title XXVI (LIHEAP) are conducted in that community.
inventory.U0023: The State plan must contain an assurance that the State will permit and cooperate with Federal investigations undertaken pursuant to section 9916 of this title.
inventory.U0024: The State plan must contain an assurance that any eligible entity that received CSBG funding in the previous fiscal year will not have its funding terminated or reduced below its previous year proportional share unless, after notice and opportunity for a hearing on the record, the State determines that cause exists, subject to review by the Secretary under section 9915(b).
inventory.U0025: The State plan must contain an assurance that the State and eligible entities will, to the maximum extent possible, coordinate programs and form partnerships with other organizations serving low-income residents, including religious organizations, charitable groups, and community organizations.
inventory.U0026: The State plan must contain an assurance that the State will require each eligible entity to establish procedures allowing a low-income individual, community organization, religious organization, or representative of low-income individuals who considers their organization or low-income individuals inadequately represented on the entity's board (or other mechanism) to petition for adequate representation.
inventory.U0027: The State plan must contain an assurance that the State will secure from each eligible entity, as a condition of receiving CSBG funding, a community action plan that includes a community-needs assessment (which may be coordinated with other assessments), and must submit that community action plan to the Secretary upon request with the State plan.
inventory.U0028: The State plan must contain an assurance that the State and all eligible entities will participate, not later than fiscal year 2001, in the Results Oriented Management and Accountability System (ROMA), another performance measurement system facilitated by the Secretary under section 9917(b), or an alternative qualifying system, and must contain a description of outcome measures used to measure entity performance in promoting self-sufficiency, family stability, and community revitalization.
inventory.U0029: The State plan must contain information describing how the State will carry out each of the assurances described in subsection (b).
inventory.U0030: For purposes of making a funding reduction determination under subsection (b)(8), 'cause' includes a statewide redistribution of CSBG funds to respond to the results of the most recently available census or other appropriate data, the designation of a new eligible entity, or severe economic dislocation.
inventory.U0031: For purposes of making a funding reduction determination under subsection (b)(8), 'cause' includes the failure of an eligible entity to comply with the terms of an agreement or State plan, or to meet a State requirement, as described in section 9915(a) of this title.
inventory.U0032: For purposes of making a funding termination determination under subsection (b)(8), 'cause' includes the failure of an eligible entity to comply with the terms of an agreement or State plan, or to meet a State requirement, as described in section 9915(a) of this title.
inventory.U0033: The Secretary is authorized to prescribe procedures for the purpose of assessing the effectiveness of eligible entities in carrying out the purposes of this chapter.
inventory.U0034: The chief executive officer of each State is permitted to revise any plan prepared under section 9908 and must submit any such revised plan to the Secretary.
inventory.U0035: Each plan or revised plan prepared under section 9908 must be made available for public inspection within the State in a manner that facilitates review of, and comment on, the plan.
inventory.U0036: For fiscal year 2000, to be eligible to receive a grant or allotment under section 9905 or 9906, a State must prepare and submit to the Secretary an application and State plan in accordance with the provisions of this chapter as in effect on October 26, 1998, rather than conforming to subsections (a) through (c).
inventory.U0037: The amendment made by Pub. L. 113-128 took effect on the first day of the first full program year after July 22, 2014 (July 1, 2015).

claim_judgments.rationale: Accurately reflects the requirement in subsection (a)(1) that the chief executive officer of a State seeking a grant or allotment designate a lead agency complying with paragraph (2) in the State application submitted under subsection (b).
Correctly captures the lead agency duty under subsection (a)(2)(A) to develop the State plan for submission to the Secretary under subsection (b).

Faithfully reflects subsection (a)(2)(B) requiring the lead agency to hold at least one public hearing with sufficient time and statewide notice regarding the proposed use and distribution of grant or allotment funds.
Faithfully captures the lead agency duty under subsection (a)(2)(C) to conduct reviews of eligible entities under section 9914.
Accurately reflects subsection (a)(3) requiring the State to hold at least one legislative hearing every 3 years in conjunction with State plan development to maintain eligibility.

Faithfully reflects the general application and plan submission requirement under subsection (b), including the effective starting point (fiscal year 2000), plan period (1 to 2 fiscal years), and 30-day pre-fiscal year submission deadline.
Accurately combines the assurance and descriptive requirements of subsection (b)(1)(A)(i)-(vii) assisting low-income individuals and families across the specified domains.
Correctly captures the plan assurance requirement in subsection (b)(1)(B) addressing the needs of youth in low-income communities through youth development programs.
Correctly reflects subsection (b)(1)(C) requiring plan assurances regarding coordinating with and making effective use of other related programs, including State welfare reform.
Faithfully reflects subsection (b)(2) requiring a description of how the State intends to use discretionary funds from the remainder of the grant or allotment described in section 9907(b).
Accurately groups the information items required under subsection (b)(3)(A)-(D) provided by eligible entities regarding service delivery, linkages, resource coordination, and innovative initiatives.
Faithfully reflects subsection (b)(4) requiring an assurance that eligible entities will provide emergency supplies, services, and nutritious food to counteract starvation and malnutrition.
Correctly reflects subsection (b)(5) requiring an assurance of service coordination/linkages to prevent duplication and a description of employment and training activity coordination under WIOA.
Faithfully reflects subsection (b)(6) requiring assurances of antipoverty program coordination and conduct of emergency energy crisis intervention programs where appropriate.
Accurately reflects subsection (b)(7) requiring an assurance that the State will permit and cooperate with Federal investigations under section 9916.

Accurately reflects subsection (b)(8) requiring an assurance protecting previously funded eligible entities from termination or proportional reduction without cause, notice, and a hearing on the record.
Accurately reflects subsection (b)(9) requiring an assurance regarding coordination and partnership with other organizations serving low-income residents to the maximum extent possible.
Accurately reflects subsection (b)(10) requiring an assurance that eligible entities establish procedures for petitioning for adequate board representation.
Accurately reflects subsection (b)(11) requiring an assurance that the State secure community action plans with community-needs assessments from eligible entities as a condition of funding.
Accurately reflects subsection (b)(12) requiring assurances of participation in ROMA or an alternative system by fiscal year 2001 and description of outcome measures.
Accurately reflects subsection (b)(13) requiring the plan to contain information describing how the State will carry out the assurances in subsection (b).
Faithfully defines 'cause' for a funding reduction under subsection (c)(1), covering both statewide redistribution circumstances and compliance/performance failures.
Faithfully defines 'cause' for a funding termination under subsection (c)(2) as failure of an eligible entity to comply with agreement, State plan, or State requirements.
Correctly captures the discretionary authority granted to the Secretary in subsection (d) to prescribe effectiveness assessment procedures.
Accurately reflects the first clause of subsection (e)(1) permitting the chief executive officer of each State to revise any plan prepared under section 9908.
Accurately reflects the mandatory second clause of subsection (e)(1) requiring submission of any revised plan to the Secretary.
Accurately reflects subsection (e)(2) requiring public inspection of plans and revised plans within the State to facilitate review and comment.
Correctly captures the transitional rule under subsection (f) for fiscal year 2000 requiring application and plan submission under prior law rather than subsections (a)-(c).
